subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make a positive Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` the default for existing unset configs, and what explicit opt-out semantics must ship with it?
rationale: The source-reproducible hardening is useful, but changing an effective sandbox default can break existing workloads and needs owner approval of the security-versus-compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema, type docs, user docs, tests, and real Docker proof show fresh and upgrade behavior plus explicit override semantics.

options.title: Keep default unset
options.body: Preserve current upgrade behavior and close or rework this PR so docs recommend operator-configured `pidsLimit` instead of changing runtime defaults.

options.title: Make strict cap opt-in
options.body: Introduce a maintainer-approved explicit strict mode or profile if hardening should be available without changing existing unset deployments.

recommendation.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema, type docs, user docs, tests, and real Docker proof show fresh and upgrade behavior plus explicit override semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the affected sandbox runtime and security documentation surfaces to this team.
